approach: Fix it where the reader's inputs are built. `referenced_jobs` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/topics.rs resolves only ids written in the request text. Make it also resolve the ids the retried job's introspection cites: the `job` of each earlier case, plus job ids in the cause, prevention, proposed request and case texts. These are carried through the existing `carry()` path, so they are redacted and carry recorded deliverables, criteria and changed files. Request-named jobs keep the existing `MAX_REFERENCED_JOBS` cap and come first. Introspection-cited jobs follow under their own cap, `MAX_CITED_JOBS`, so the cap never drops a request-named job. The reader brief's "Referenced jobs" section prints each job's recorded criteria and deliverables and tells the reader to take fixtures, sizes and thresholds from them. The "Previous result and change scope" intro gains one sentence saying only the retried and followed-up jobs must be accounted for. `continued_jobs`, `check_prior_result_and_scope` and `refusing_check` are untouched, so nothing new is refused and no refusal share applies. `ReaderInputs` keeps its shape and no prompt file changes.

decisions.choice: Extend `referenced_jobs` to take the retried `Option<&EarlierAttempt>` instead of `skip: Option<&str>`, and read the ids from `attempt.introspection` (RetryCause) via a new pure helper `introspection_cited_ids`.
decisions.reason: The ids are lost exactly there. `RetryCause.earlier_cases[].job` already holds them (retry.rs:171-181) and `read_once` already has `attempt` (reading.rs:579). The one resolver and the one `carry()` path (redaction, bounds) are reused, and nothing new is stored.

rejected.option: A new resolver or a new `ReaderInputs` field for cited jobs
rejected.why: Duplicates `carry()`. Adds a second construction site to keep in step (reading.rs:609, briefs.rs:3430). The accepted reading says to extend the existing path.

rejected.option: A refusal rule that rejects readings whose fixtures differ from recorded jobs
rejected.why: The request prefers giving the stage the information. The recorded shape is now in the reader's brief, so no rule is needed. A rule would also need a stated refused share and a corpus case.

decisions.choice: Cap request-named jobs at `MAX_REFERENCED_JOBS` (3) as today and add `MAX_CITED_JOBS = 4` for introspection-cited jobs, listed after the request-named ones.
decisions.reason: A real retry cites 1 job in the request and 3 earlier cases in the introspection (this very failure class). One shared cap of 3 would drop a recorded shape. Listing request-named jobs first and counting them separately means the cap never drops a request-named job, which criterion 3 requires.

rejected.option: One shared cap of 3, introspection ids last
rejected.why: Drops cited jobs in the common case of 1 request id plus 3 earlier cases.
Bloats the reader brief, because each carried job brings findings and up to 30 changed files.

decisions.choice: Keep the cited jobs in the same `referenced_jobs` vector and let `continued_jobs` (filter by `followed_up_ids`) decide which must be accounted for. Add one sentence to the "Previous result and change scope" intro saying so.
decisions.reason: This keeps `check_prior_result_and_scope` and `refusing_check` unchanged, with no new refusal. The sentence stops the brief from implying the reader must account for every cited job, which `continued_jobs` (topics.rs:512-526) does not require.

rejected.why: It says the reading is refused unless it accounts for each job below, which is false for cited-only jobs and would push readers to restate unrelated work.

decisions.choice: Print the recorded criteria and deliverables inside "Referenced jobs". Changed files stay in the existing carried_work block of the "Previous result and change scope" entry for the same job.

Adding criteria and deliverables beside the request gives the reader the shape under the cited-jobs heading. Not repeating the up-to-30 changed files keeps the brief small. No line starting `Job ` is added in `carried_work`, which the fake reader at fake.rs:243 parses.

risks.risk: The reader brief grows. Each extra carried job adds its request, findings (failed-check tails are bounded to 1024 bytes each), up to 30 changed files and the new criteria and deliverables lists. With up to 3 request-named and 4 cited jobs, the brief could reach 7 jobs.
risks.mitigation: `MAX_CITED_JOBS = 4` bounds the addition. Every field goes through `carry()`, which already bounds and redacts. Changed files are not repeated in the new section. The brief sits outside the prompt-set budgets (docs/system-facts.md).

risks.risk: A reader reading "Previous result and change scope" might think it must account for each cited job and restate unrelated work, which would raise refusals by the existing check.
risks.mitigation: The added intro sentence says only the retried job and the jobs the request says it follows up must be accounted for. `continued_jobs` still filters by `followed_up_ids`, and the new corpus case and the existing follow-up case pin both outcomes.

risks.risk: Job ids in introspection prose may name jobs that are unrelated, such as a job mentioned in passing in the cause text. They would be carried but never accounted for.
risks.mitigation: Ids in `earlier_cases[].job` go first, then ids in the cause, prevention and proposed request, then ids in case texts. Ids in no record are ignored, and `MAX_CITED_JOBS` stops the list at 4.

risks.risk: The new topics.rs tests depend on helpers in the reading.rs test module, which couples two test modules.
risks.mitigation: The helpers become `pub(super)` inside `#[cfg(test)]` only. Production visibility does not change.

risks.risk: The README still says "At most three jobs are carried" (README.md:72), which is no longer the whole story, because up to four more may be carried when an introspection cites them. README.md is not a deliverable of this reading.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG entry states the second cap. The README sentence stays true for request-named jobs. Nothing reads it in a test.

risks.risk: The criterion 1 test does not compile against the base `referenced_jobs` signature, so "fails without the change" is shown by a compile error, not an assertion.
risks.mitigation: Criteria 2 and 3(ii) are behavior tests that compile on the base and fail on it by assertion. The verifier's revert run covers criterion 1.
